status: defined: inputs, assertion vocabularies and negative controls are frozen here; no oracle was executed in CE-00.2
policy: Each oracle answers one question from its own inputs. Expected values are authored in the corpus manifest from the reference outcome; they are never generated from, regenerated against or blessed from compiler output.

An oracle reads the rendered page through the browser, never compiler internals, generated declarations or the design-system definition. The implementation under test is reached only through an adapter, as in the semantic migration oracle (docs/architecture/semantic-oracle-v1.md).

Results stay separate per outcome class. A fixture can be compiler-accepted and still fail fidelity, or fail acceptance because of a vocabulary gap while the behavior itself is unsupported. No combined score or percentage is derived.
Every oracle has a negative control: a mutation of the reference that must make the oracle fail. An oracle whose negative control passes is broken, and its positive results are void.
Engines, viewports, fonts and host identities come from the CE-01 browser-profile decisions and the CE-13 host qualification. A result without the exact engine identity is not evidence.

outcomeClasses.compiler-accepted: E2: the compiler admits the fixture's authored vocabulary without diagnostics.
outcomeClasses.compiler-rejected: E2: the compiler rejects the source with the expected structured diagnostic. Expected for negative fixtures.
outcomeClasses.vocabulary-gap: The catalog or design system cannot yet express a declaration of the reference. Required work, not a failure of the reference; measured by the classifier against a named policy or catalog.
outcomeClasses.unsupported-behavior: The behavior is outside what a static, finite system or the target engine supports (registry limitations, target decisions). Reported as a limitation, never approximated and labeled equivalent.
outcomeClasses.fidelity-pass: E3/E4: the emitted CSS and the rendered page satisfy every assertion of the oracle.
outcomeClasses.fidelity-failure: E3/E4: at least one assertion fails on an accepted build.

states.pointer-hover: A mouse pointer rests over the target (real pointer move, not a forced pseudo-class).
states.pointer-active: The primary mouse button is held down on the target.
states.touch: Emulated coarse pointer without hover (pointer: coarse, hover: none) and touch input events.
states.keyboard-focus: The target received focus from Tab or Shift+Tab, so :focus-visible matches.
states.keyboard-navigation: Arrow, Home, End, Enter or Space keys move focus or activate inside a composite widget.
states.error: The control carries aria-invalid="true" and an associated error message.
states.loading: The control or region carries aria-busy="true".
states.disabled: The control is disabled natively or with aria-disabled="true".
states.increased-contrast: The user prefers more contrast (prefers-contrast: more).
states.reduced-motion: The user prefers reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).
states.scrolled: A scroll container was scrolled by a stated offset.
states.rtl: Right-to-left direction from the document or an ancestor dir attribute.
states.hydrated: After client hydration or a client-side route change of a server-rendered page.

oracles.question: Does the compiler admit the fixture when the design system authorizes exactly the listed vocabulary, and reject it with the expected diagnostic when one item is withdrawn?
inputs: fixture acceptedVocabulary (tokens, conditions, resources)
fixture source written against the canonical authoring API of the owning lot
compiler package identity and design-system definition digest
procedure: Compile the fixture source with a definition that declares exactly the listed vocabulary; require zero diagnostics.
For each listed item, compile again with that item withdrawn; require a structured rejection naming the missing item.
oracles.independence: The vocabulary list is authored from the reference outcome, not read from a definition the compiler produced.
oracles.negativeControl: Withdraw one authorized token or condition; a run that still reports zero diagnostics fails the oracle.

oracles.question: Is every declaration of the reference stylesheet emitted, under an equivalent condition, after the single target transform?
inputs: reference stylesheet(s) and their accounting in accounting.v1.json
emitted and target-transformed CSS of the build
browser target decision of the bound profile
procedure: Canonicalize both stylesheets with the same parser: expand shorthands to longhands, normalize colors and lengths, map conditions to their media or selector meaning.
Require each reference longhand under each reference condition to have exactly one emitted counterpart with an equal canonical value.
Require that the emitted CSS adds no declaration whose computed effect differs on the fixture's elements.
oracles.independence: Reference declarations come from the authored stylesheet; emitted CSS is only compared, never used to update the reference.
oracles.negativeControl: Delete one reference declaration from the emitted CSS; the oracle must report the missing longhand and condition.

oracles.question: Do the targets have the expected border boxes, positions, scroll and stacking behavior at each viewport and state?
inputs: built page and the reference page, each served with the fixture CSP
viewports and states of the assertion
exact engine identity
procedure: Render at the viewport, drive the state with real input, wait for fonts and two animation frames.
Read getBoundingClientRect, scroll extents and elementFromPoint for each target; compare with the expectation within the tolerance.
oracles.comparator: Pixel values compare within tolerancePx (default 0.5). Expected numbers are authored from fixed sizes, so they do not depend on fonts.
oracles.independence: Expectations are authored numbers or the rendered reference page; the oracle never reads class names, generated CSS or definitions.
oracles.negativeControl: Remove the reference's grid-template-columns (or the target's width) declaration; the box assertion must fail.

oracles.question: Does text wrap, truncate, preserve breaks, isolate direction and flow vertically as specified?
inputs: built page and reference page
viewports and states of the assertion
exact engine identity and, for font-dependent metrics, a pinned font resource
procedure: Measure line boxes with Range.getClientRects per target, compare scrollWidth with clientWidth, read computed direction and writing mode.

Font-dependent assertions require the pinned font of the executing lot; assertions in this corpus are font-independent by construction (single line versus several lines, truncation, preserved author breaks, overflow).
oracles.comparator: Integer line counts compare exactly or against a stated minimum. Edge positions compare within tolerancePx.
oracles.independence: Expected line behavior comes from the authored text and sizes, not from a rendering of the build.
oracles.negativeControl: Replace white-space: pre-line by normal (or remove text-overflow: ellipsis); the line or truncation assertion must fail.

oracles.question: Does each state produce the expected computed styles, and only in that state?
inputs: built page and reference page
states driven by real input or by the documented ARIA attributes
media emulation for touch, reduced motion, forced colors, contrast and print
procedure: Read computed styles of the target at rest, enter the state with real input or media emulation, read again.
Require the expected values in the state and the rest values outside it.
oracles.comparator: Computed values compare after the browser's own serialization; colors as resolved sRGB or system color keywords.
oracles.independence: States are entered with real pointer, keyboard and media emulation; forcing pseudo-classes through developer protocol is not accepted.
oracles.negativeControl: Delete the reference's :focus-visible outline rule; the focus state assertion must fail.

oracles.question: Can the page be operated by keyboard alone, with a visible focus indicator at every step?
inputs: built page and reference page
key sequence of the assertion
procedure: Start from the document, press the keys of the sequence through the browser input pipeline.
After each step record document.activeElement, whether :focus-visible matches and the focus indicator's painted outline or box-shadow area.
oracles.comparator: The first Tab stops, starting from the document, must equal the listed targets in order; later stops are not constrained. :focus-visible matching is not enough. At every stop the focused element (or, when it is visually hidden, its next sibling) needs a visible indicator: an outline that is not none, has non-zero width and a color with alpha above 0; a box shadow that focus added or changed, with alpha above 0 and a non-zero offset, blur or spread; or a changed border side that is not none, has non-zero width and alpha above 0. In addition, at least 40 pixels must change between the focused and unfocused screenshots inside the indicator ring: the border box grown by the indicator extent plus 8px, minus the content box.
oracles.independence: Sequences are authored from the reference markup; the oracle never relies on generated class names.
oracles.negativeControl: Swap the tabindex of two targets, remove every focus indicator, or make it transparent (`outline: 3px solid transparent`); the order or painted-indicator assertion must fail.

oracles.question: Do styling outcomes preserve roles, names, contrast, target size and forced-colors visibility?
inputs: built page and reference page
browser accessibility tree snapshot
states including high-contrast and increased-contrast
procedure: Read the accessibility tree for role and name of each target.
Compute contrast from computed colors against the effective background; measure target sizes; in forced colors require visible boundaries.
oracles.comparator: Contrast uses the WCAG 2.2 relative luminance formula; sizes in CSS pixels.
oracles.independence: Roles and names come from authored markup; contrast and size thresholds are WCAG 2.2 values.
oracles.negativeControl: Set the error text color to the background color, or hide the label with display: none; the contrast or name assertion must fail.

oracles.question: Does the page render completely under a restrictive CSP without inline styles, injected style elements or runtime style transport?
inputs: built page served with the fixture policy as an HTTP header
securitypolicyviolation events, DOM snapshot after interaction
host identity (CE-13) for E5 qualification
procedure: Load every route of the fixture, run each assertion's states, then collect violations.
Count <style> elements, [style] attributes, CSSOM insertions made at runtime and custom properties set on elements by script.
oracles.comparator: All counters compare exactly with zero unless the assertion states otherwise.
oracles.independence: The policy text is authored in the manifest; the oracle observes the browser, not the build output.
oracles.negativeControl: Add one style attribute or one injected <style> element to the page; the violation or counter assertion must fail.
